text: Reproduce: `su - reportbot -c 'echo ok'` prints `su: failed to execute /usr/local/sbin/corp-shell: No such file or directory`. That's an exec() failure, not a permissions message and not nologin's canned text -- the file su is trying to run doesn't exist at all.

Confirm the configured shell: `getent passwd reportbot` -- last field is `/usr/local/sbin/corp-shell`. Check whether it's actually there: `ls -l /usr/local/sbin/corp-shell` (or just `test -x /usr/local/sbin/corp-shell; echo $?`).
The wrapper binary is gone and there's no package or fixture available to reinstall it in this box. The practical fix is to point reportbot at a real, existing shell instead.
`sudo usermod -s /bin/bash reportbot`. Verify with `su - reportbot -c 'echo ok'`.
